name: Stanford Pupper
def: Open source servo driven quadruped derived from Stanford Doggo and designed as a teaching kit for legged robotics courses.
body: Pupper is much smaller and cheaper than Doggo, using twelve hobby scale actuators, a Raspberry Pi and a small motor controller board. Its published bill of materials, printed parts and Python control stack let students build a trotting robot in a weekend and then modify the controller. It is used in university courses and workshops, and later revisions moved to brushless motors for more dynamic behaviour.
facts: Designed as a low cost teaching kit and used in university legged robotics courses
Design and software published openly, spawning many derivative kits
specs: Hobby scale servo actuators, three per leg
Python gait controller on a Raspberry Pi with game controller input
